key_insight: A hybrid cross-modal attention model that combines mammograms with clinical data can improve early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help support more accurate, context-aware screening where radiology expertise and high-quality imaging are limited.
method: Trained a transformer-based cross-modal attention network on mammograms plus structured clinical features.
Used a locally collected dataset from 4 Ethiopian referral hospitals with biopsy-confirmed labels.
Compared against image-only baselines and assessed robustness to low-quality images.
evidence_signal: On 2,560 mammogram images from 1,024 patients, the model reached 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and 0.987 AUC.
watch_item: Results come from a locally collected dataset, so external validation is still needed before broad deployment.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
